note: 2026-09-16 demo-booking PR-1 (feat/demo-booking-api, two Opus review rounds, 13 findings fixed) lesson candidate, HELD per the same 'ids come from the lead' convention other sessions in this register have followed -- register is 51/52 active near the byte cap, authority not capacity is the blocker: 'two independent race guards that each key/constrain on a DIFFERENT dimension of the same conflict can both individually hold while the real conflict still occurs -- an advisory lock keyed on a slot's exact START INSTANT and a DB unique index on that same START column both looked sufficient, but neither is an INTERVAL-overlap constraint: a slot-interval config shorter than the appointment duration let the grid offer two different starts (10:00 and 10:15 for a 30-minute slot) whose actual time ranges overlap, taking different lock keys and satisfying the index trivially. When a lock key or a unique constraint is chosen to guard a conflict, ask whether the conflict is actually keyed on IDENTITY (exact match, which a lock/index on that field genuinely covers) or on OVERLAP (a range/interval, which needs either a range constraint or an upstream invariant that the values compared can never legitimately overlap in the first place) -- this project's second confirmed case of that mismatch class after the round-1 db-locks contention work.' Secondary, smaller candidate from the same PR: a `\uXXXX`-style escape sequence typed into an Edit/Write tool's string content can land in the target file as a RAW byte instead of the literal 6-character escape sequence -- caught only because `file` reported the .ts source as "data" instead of text; already reserved as L-174 by routeflow-c4/the lead for the register session to write, not duplicated here. 2026-09-15 PR-1a fix-round commit 046f0a85 (feat/returns-inline-pr1a, independent Opus refute-first review of 2b75438) -- TWO MORE lesson candidates, both HELD for the same reason as the entry immediately below (ids come from the lead, register is 49/52 active with capacity free, authority not capacity is the blocker): (F1) a money-basis defect from a HALF-applied accounting fix -- create()'s over-return cap was changed to SUM a product's qty across every live order line (the entry below), but the sibling pricing code (priceReturn's never-invoiced branch) that must agree with that same cap kept pricing off a single matched line's rate against the now-pooled qty, over-crediting a product split across two differently-priced lines. Candidate lesson: 'when a guard/cap computation is widened to pool across multiple rows for one key, grep every OTHER reader of that same key (in this case, the sibling pricing function) that assumed a single row -- a cap and a price computed from different bases silently mismatch, and the mismatch is a MONEY bug, not a correctness one.' (F2) a filter that only ever ran against a mock -- returns-pieces.util.ts's CANCELLED-line exclusion referenced `li.status`, but none of the four real Prisma `order.lineItems` selects in returns.service.ts fetched `status` -- the exclusion was dead code against a live database from the moment it was written, and the ORIGINAL test for it passed anyway because its mock object supplied `status` directly, never proving the real select clause produced it. This is the SAME shape as the already-noted-but-unminted 'shared helper that re-derives a precondition...' candidate several notes below (statement.service.ts, 2026-09-15) -- a strong signal these two sessions independently hit the identical class of defect and it may be worth one shared lesson id covering both call sites when the lead mints. Confirmed via `git show origin/master:apps/api/src/returns/returns.service.ts` that F2 does NOT reproduce on master independently of this PR -- the CANCELLED-exclusion concept is new to this PR, so master has no equivalent no-op filter; not filed as a registry bug. Older note below (also this PR-1a branch, commit 2b75438) preserved verbatim. 2026-09-15 PR-1a (Returns Inside Order Creation, feat/returns-inline-pr1a) lesson candidate, HELD per the lead's own PR-1a ruling that ids (bugs, lessons) come from the lead -- not minted here: returns.service.ts create()'s over-return guard computed 'sold qty for (order, product)' via `.find()`, picking a single order line for the product and silently ignoring every OTHER line for the same product on the same order (a re-added line, a post-edit split) -- undercounting what was actually sold and refusing legitimate returns. Candidate lesson: 'when an accounting total for a KEY (order, product) can legitimately be spread across MORE THAN ONE row (multiple lines, multiple sources), grep for every writer that could produce a second row for the same key before trusting a `.find()`/`first()` lookup -- sum across all live rows for that key instead, the same way a money total is never read off a single row when more than one can exist.' Fixed via a new shared soldPiecesForProduct (returns-pieces.util.ts) that sums every non-CANCELLED OrderItem line for the product; no prior lesson (L-096/L-119/L-125 are adjacent but not this pattern) already covers it. Register is 49/52 active with 3 slots free -- capacity is not the blocker here, id-minting authority is.
